bahrain.title: MPs propose up to five years in jail and BD 50,000 fine for harmful AI deepfakes
bahrain.summary: Five MPs want the Information Technology Crimes Law amended so that creating fake AI images, audio or video of a real person that breach their privacy carries jail and a fine of up to BD 30,000. Publishing the material, or using it to blackmail, threaten or defame, would raise the maximum to five years and BD 50,000.

bahrain.title: World Bank sees Gulf economies shrinking 4.3 per cent in 2026, then rebounding
bahrain.summary: The World Bank projects GCC growth of 10.3 per cent in 2027 if the conflict involving Iran eases and oil output and shipping return to normal, after a 4.3 per cent contraction this year. Bahrain is forecast to grow 4.2 per cent in 2027, behind Qatar at 26.7 per cent, Kuwait at 22 per cent and the UAE at 9.5 per cent.

bahrain.title: EWA to study keeping electricity subsidy for families after an account holder dies
bahrain.summary: The Electricity and Water Authority told the Southern Municipal Council that families have 90 days to adjust an account after a death before the subsidy is removed, and that it will examine a council proposal on continuing the subsidy. Councillors also urged checks on unusually high bills and merging the first two subsidised tariff bands.

bahrain.title: LMRA deported 547 workers in September after 4,675 inspection visits
bahrain.summary: The Labour Market Regulatory Authority carried out 4,675 inspection visits and 172 joint campaigns last month, detaining 67 irregular workers and deporting 547. Since January 2024 there have been 145,607 visits and 15,210 deportations, and the authority says campaigns will intensify across all governorates.

bahrain.title: Bahrain Bourse index falls for a third month as property deals drop 63 per cent
bahrain.summary: The All Share Index lost 1.5 per cent in September to close at 1,907.8 points, taking its third quarter decline to 6.6 per cent, according to Kamco Invest. Real estate was the only sector to gain, up 12.3 per cent. Land registry data shows property transactions fell 63.2 per cent in the first half of 2026 to 4,951, worth BD 671 million.

bahrain.title: Saudi Arabia and UAE account for 83 per cent of Bahrain's Gulf trade
bahrain.summary: Bahrain Chamber figures put trade with the rest of the GCC at $8.73 billion last year, with Saudi Arabia at $3.93 billion and the UAE at $3.33 billion. Qatar, Oman and Kuwait together made up about $1.47 billion. Saudis were also 10.4 million of the 11.2 million GCC citizen arrivals in 2025.

bahrain.title: First Made in GCC forum and exhibition opens at Exhibition World Bahrain
bahrain.summary: The inaugural Made in GCC 2026 Forum and Exhibition opened on 6 October in the presence of the Crown Prince and Prime Minister. The Industry and Commerce Minister said it is meant to build a unified Gulf industrial brand, attract investment and raise manufacturing's share of the region's economies.

bahrain.title: Council chief wants water tanks and heaters fitted just before housing handover
bahrain.summary: The Southern Municipal Council chairman proposed installing tanks and heaters in new government homes one month before handover, since warranties of three to five years can run out before families move in. The Housing Ministry rejected a separate tank cooler proposal on cost grounds, noting about 48,000 families are on waiting lists.

crypto.title: Bitcoin slips below $84,000 as Iranian tanker attacks lift oil and bond yields
crypto.summary: Bitcoin fell to about $83,840 on Wednesday after trading near $86,600 a day earlier, as Brent rose to about $101.50 and the US 10-year yield reached 5.31 per cent. Roughly $550 million in long positions were liquidated in 24 hours, and ether, XRP and dogecoin fell 3 to 5 per cent.

crypto.title: House finance chair says SEC and CFTC rules are no substitute for the CLARITY Act
crypto.summary: Representative French Hill said rulemaking proposed by the two regulators after the Senate failed to pass the market structure bill last month falls short of permanent law. He hopes it can pass in the lame duck session, when the Senate will sit for only 22 days after the November midterms.

crypto.title: Coinbase completes Deribit integration, giving US clients offshore derivatives access
crypto.summary: Eligible US institutions can now reach Deribit's options and perpetual futures through Coinbase's CFTC-regulated derivatives unit, without needing offshore entities. Options on Coinbase Prime are due in the coming weeks, with US retail access planned later this year. Coinbase says derivatives are about 80 per cent of global crypto volume.

crypto.title: Bitmine to stop buying ether once it holds 5 per cent of supply
crypto.summary: Chairman Tom Lee said the largest Ethereum treasury company will end its weekly purchases at 5 per cent of circulating supply. It holds 6,016,414 ETH, about 4.9 per cent, and needs roughly 100,000 more. The move removes a steady buyer that has purchased every week since June 2025. Ether fell 5 per cent on the day.

crypto.title: Russia registers its first licensed crypto exchanges and custodians
crypto.summary: The Bank of Russia listed four exchange operators and five custodians under the crypto law that took effect on 1 September, including Sberbank as a custodian and VTB on both lists. Sberbank plans to launch products for Bitcoin, Ether and USDT on 1 December. Paying for goods with crypto remains banned.

crypto.title: Pudgy Penguins owner to shut its Abstract blockchain on 15 December
crypto.summary: Igloo is closing the Ethereum layer 2 network after spending tens of millions of dollars on it over about 18 months, citing stalled growth and fee income too low to cover costs. About $76 million remains on the chain and users must move assets before the shutdown. It is the second Ethereum layer 2 to announce closure in a week.
